With Fathom Seer and Riptide Survivor already on board as morph creatures that can generate card advantage, and with Well of Ideas (6 mana) being the likely payoff to ramp toward, Ur-Golem's Eye is defensible. However, Concentrate draws 3 cards immediately at the same mana cost, which could find lands and more options. The player already has 5 lands (4 Islands + Myriad Landscape) and the Eye only adds colorless mana. Drawing 3 cards with Concentrate would likely find more lands naturally while also finding action, and the board doesn't require urgent ramping since there's no 6-drop that must come down next turn. The ramp play is reasonable but drawing 3 is generally stronger in a deck that wants to find answers and threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ur-Golem's Eye for colorless mana ramp
annotations.betterLine: Cast Concentrate to draw 3 cards, finding more options and likely hitting land drops naturally while maintaining card advantage

annotations.description: Cast Grave Pact with zero creatures on board while having a severe green mana deficit (no green-producing basic lands, only Command Tower and Rupture Spire for green). Grave Pact does nothing without creatures to trigger it.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Grave Pact (1BBB) with no creatures on the battlefield
annotations.betterLine: Cast Cultivate (2G) to search for Forests, fixing the critical green mana shortage and enabling future plays like Yavimaya Elder. Grave Pact could be deployed later once creatures are established to trigger it.

annotations.description: Discarding Concentrate to Syphon Mind instead of the basic Island. With 4 Islands, Myriad Landscape, and Ur-Golem's Eye already in play (providing 8+ mana), the 5th Island provides marginal value compared to a spell that draws 3 cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Concentrate, keeping Island in hand along with Cyclonic Rift and Well of Ideas.
annotations.betterLine: Discard the basic Island instead. ESPN already has sufficient mana to cast all remaining spells and doesn't need another land. Concentrate (draw 3) provides far more value than an extra Island at this stage.

annotations.description: Casting Divine Reckoning destroys the player's own Talrand, Sky Summoner (a key value engine that creates Drake tokens from instants/sorceries) to deal with relatively low-threat creatures (Fathom Seer 1/3 and Riptide Survivor 2/1). The opponent ESPN keeps one creature anyway. Meanwhile, Talrand is the most valuable creature on the board for Grok4F's game plan. Additionally, casting Divine Reckoning before combat means Talrand doesn't get to create a Drake token from the spell (Divine Reckoning is a sorcery, so Talrand would trigger - but the Drake would then be destroyed by Divine Reckoning since the player would likely keep Talrand over a fresh 2/2 Drake). Actually, Talrand triggers when the spell is cast, creating a Drake before Divine Reckoning resolves. The player could then keep Talrand and sacrifice the Drake. So they keep Talrand and ESPN keeps one creature. This is more reasonable than it first appears - they clear one of ESPN's morph creatures. However, using a board wipe when you have the best creature and opponents have minimal boards seems premature. The Myriad Landscape activation could have been used instead to ramp, saving Divine Reckoning for when opponents develop more threatening boards.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Divine Reckoning, destroying most creatures on board while keeping Talrand (since the Drake token from Talrand's trigger gives a choice to keep Talrand).
annotations.betterLine: Activate Myriad Landscape to ramp (search for two basic lands), saving Divine Reckoning for a turn when opponents have developed more threatening boards. The current opposing creatures (Fathom Seer and Riptide Survivor) are not major threats worth spending a board wipe on.

annotations.description: With 8 mana available (4 Islands + Ur-Golem's Eye + Myriad Landscape), the player could cast Concentrate (2UU) to draw 3 cards and still have mana left over, or cast Crown of Doom (3) to develop the board. Activating Myriad Landscape costs 2 mana plus sacrificing the land and tapping it, fetching two basic lands tapped. While ramp is fine, the player already has 6 mana sources (4 Islands + Ur-Golem's Eye + Myriad Landscape) and has powerful spells to cast. Casting Concentrate this turn would draw 3 cards, potentially finding more lands and action, while still being able to activate Myriad Landscape on a future turn. The sequencing of ramping before casting a draw spell when you already have sufficient mana for your hand's spells is slightly suboptimal - Concentrate would give more options and the ramp could wait since the player isn't close to casting Well of Ideas (6 mana) this turn anyway. However, after sacrificing Myriad Landscape, the player loses a mana source this turn, making it harder to cast Concentrate. With Myriad Landscape tapped for the activation, the player would have only 4 Islands + Ur-Golem's Eye = 6 mana minus 2 for activation = 4 mana remaining, which is exactly enough for Concentrate (2UU). Actually, the activation costs {2}, {T}, sacrifice - so they tap Myriad Landscape and pay 2 from other sources, leaving 4 mana (2 Islands + Ur-Golem's Eye for 2). That's only 4 mana with just 2 blue - not enough for Concentrate (2UU needs at least 2U from Islands). So activating Myriad Landscape first prevents casting Concentrate this turn. Casting Concentrate first and then activating Myriad Landscape next turn would have been better sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Myriad Landscape to search for two basic lands, using up mana that could have been spent on Concentrate.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Concentrate (2UU) using 4 Islands to draw 3 cards, then activate Myriad Landscape next turn. This maximizes information and card advantage before committing to ramp.

All opponents are at 40 life, so the damage is minimal, but in a multiplayer game there's usually little reason not to send small creatures at an open opponent. GPT5m Timmy has no creatures and only 3 lands (Swamp, Forest, Radiant Fountain) - they can't block. Attacking Timmy for 3 damage is free value with no risk. The creatures don't have any particular defensive value to hold back since no opponent has threatening attackers yet.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with either creature.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GPT5m Timmy (who has no blockers) with both Fathom Seer and Riptide Survivor for 3 damage. There's no downside to this attack and it chips away at an opponent's life total.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Myriad Landscape (paying {2} with Ur-Golem's Eye) to search for two basic Islands, gaining ramp while still holding up mana for Cyclonic Rift

Cultivate costs {2}{G} - they could pay with Temple (2 colorless) + Forest (G) = exactly 3 mana for Cultivate. This would ramp them significantly, fixing their mana and putting them ahead on lands. They control 7 lands total (5 tapped from earlier plays, 2 untapped), so Temple of the False God is active. Casting Cultivate here would search for two basics, putting one onto the battlefield tapped and the other into hand, accelerating toward expensive threats like Scythe Specter next turn. Declining to cast it wastes available mana this turn.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Cultivate using Temple of the False God (2) + Forest (G) to ramp and fix mana, setting up a stronger next turn with more lands available for Scythe Specter or other plays.

annotations.description: In a multiplayer game, attacking the weakest player (GPT5m Timmy with only 3 lands and no board presence) rather than Sonnet Gramps who has Grave Pact - a very dangerous enchantment that threatens Grok4F's creature-based strategy with Talrand - is strategically questionable. Applying pressure to the biggest threat is generally correct multiplayer strategy.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT5m Timmy, the weakest player at the table with minimal board presence.
annotations.betterLine: Attack Sonnet Gramps, who controls Grave Pact and represents the biggest strategic threat to Grok4F's Talrand token strategy.

annotations.description: Gem25F ESPN declined to activate Myriad Landscape during Grok4F Analyst's postcombat main phase. This is an opponent's turn, so activating Myriad Landscape here would be optimal timing — it uses mana that would otherwise go unused (they have no other instant-speed plays worth holding up besides Cyclonic Rift), and fetching two basic Islands would thin the deck and ramp for next turn. With a hand containing Concentrate (4 mana), Well of Ideas (6 mana), and Crown of Doom (3 mana), ramping is important. The 2 mana activation cost plus sacrificing the land is easily affordable, and doing it on an opponent's turn means the lands enter tapped but are ready to untap on ESPN's next turn. Holding up Cyclonic Rift (2 mana) is reasonable but there's no immediate threat worth bouncing — Talrand just attacked and the board isn't threatening enough to warrant holding up a single-target bounce over ramping.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Myriad Landscape
annotations.betterLine: Activate Myriad Landscape to search for two basic Islands, ramping from 6 mana-producing lands + Ur-Golem's Eye to 7 lands + Eye, enabling Well of Ideas or Concentrate + Crown of Doom next turn

annotations.description: Crown of Doom is a risky play in this board state. It gives +2/+0 to any creature attacking Gem25F ESPN, making them more vulnerable to attacks. Additionally, all of Gem25F ESPN's lands are tapped, so they can't hold up Cyclonic Rift for protection. With Sonnet Gramps having Grave Pact on board (a threatening enchantment), and face-down morphs ready to flip, the board position doesn't favor inviting attacks.

annotations.actionTaken: Passed on declaring any attackers

annotations.description: Casting Yavimaya Elder (a creature) in the precombat main phase when there's no reason to do so before combat. With Grave Pact on the battlefield, the Elder could potentially be sacrificed for value, but more importantly, casting creatures before combat gives opponents information and doesn't leverage any haste or ETB combat effects. Additionally, the player could have considered casting Cultivate instead to ramp and thin the deck, since they already have Buried Alive targets in the graveyard and may want to cast The Mimeoplasm soon (which costs 2BGU). However, the bigger issue is sequencing - playing Dimir Aqueduct first (as the land drop) would have been better to set up future mana, since the Elder doesn't need to come down this turn specifically. The player also should have considered that they could play Dimir Aqueduct, bounce a tapped land, and still have mana for Cultivate or Sign in Blood instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Yavimaya Elder for 1GG using remaining untapped lands after Buried Alive resolved.
annotations.betterLine: Play Dimir Aqueduct as the land drop (bouncing a tapped Swamp), then cast Cultivate with the available mana (Command Tower + Forest + Rupture Spire = 1GG) to ramp toward casting The Mimeoplasm sooner, fixing mana along the way. Alternatively, cast Sign in Blood to dig for more cards while keeping mana development options open.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Faithless Looting first (triggers Talrand for a 2/2 Drake token, draws 2 cards for better information), then cast Dockside Extortionist and make remaining plays based on new cards drawn.

Discarding it over less critical cards like Essence Pulse (situational sweeper) or Alhammarret's Archive (expensive win-more artifact) loses significant long-term value.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Essence Pulse and Alhammarret's Archive (or Essence Pulse and Moldervine Reclamation), keeping Well of Lost Dreams as the premier card-draw engine for the life-gain strategy

annotations.description: Attacking with all creatures including Fathom Seer (1/3) and Riptide Survivor (2/1) is risky given Sonnet Gramps has Grave Pact on the battlefield. If any of ESPN's creatures die in combat, Grave Pact doesn't trigger (it's Gramps's enchantment), but the fragile creatures are being sent into combat unnecessarily. More importantly, Sonnet Gramps has Brawn and Wonder in graveyard with a Forest in play, meaning any creatures Gramps controls would have trample and flying. The real concern is that attacking with all creatures leaves no blockers, and with only 7 lands + Ur-Golem's Eye, ESPN is tapping out offensively when they have Cyclonic Rift and Exclude in hand as defensive options they'd want mana for. However, the creatures are currently untapped and the mana artifacts/lands are already tapped, so holding back creatures as blockers while having countermagic available on opponents' turns could be more prudent. Sphinx of Jwar Isle (5/5 flying shroud) is the safe attacker; the smaller creatures risk trading poorly.

Casting it as a morph preserves the option to turn it face up later to skip all opponents' untap steps - a powerful tempo swing. Casting it face-up is just a vanilla 5/4, wasting its most impactful ability. With 8 mana available (4 Islands + Ur-Golem's Eye), casting it face-down for 3 would leave 5 mana open for Cyclonic Rift or Exclude as interaction, or could cast Shaper Parasite face-down as well.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brine Elemental face-up for 4UU, using most of their mana and losing the morph trigger entirely.

annotations.description: Brine Elemental is on the stack being cast by an opponent. This is a very dangerous creature - when turned face up (or cast normally and later flickered/recast face-down), it causes each opponent to skip their next untap step. More importantly, it's a 5/4 body. Gem25F ESPN has Exclude in hand which counters target creature spell AND draws a card. This is a clean 2-for-1 against a significant threat. Sonnet Gramps has Grave Pact on the battlefield and Brawn/Wonder in graveyard, meaning their creatures are especially dangerous. Letting a 5/4 resolve when you have a hard counter that also cantrips is a significant missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to respond to Brine Elemental on the stack, letting it resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Exclude targeting Brine Elemental to counter it and draw a card. This removes a meaningful threat while replacing itself, which is pure value.

Bouncing the Aqueduct to 'get more value' is actually less value - you lose the Aqueduct's mana production this turn cycle and will need to bounce yet another land when you replay it.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Dimir Aqueduct with Golgari Rot Farm's ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Bounce a basic Swamp instead, preserving Dimir Aqueduct's mana production and avoiding the chain of bounce-land bouncing bounce-land tempo loss

annotations.betterLine: Consider using Exclude to counter Yavimaya Elder, denying the Grave Pact synergy and drawing a card in the process. The value denial plus card draw makes Exclude efficient here.

annotations.description: During the draw step, Sonnet Gramps declined to cast Fact or Fiction with an opponent's Well of Ideas on the stack. Fact or Fiction is an instant that could be cast at this point, and with Well of Ideas about to resolve (which will give all opponents extra cards), casting Fact or Fiction now before the main phase is essentially equivalent to casting it during the main phase in terms of card advantage. However, there's a subtle consideration: if Well of Ideas resolves, it draws Sonnet Gramps 2 cards on entry, and then during their draw step they'll draw 2 additional cards. Casting Fact or Fiction now vs. later during the turn doesn't change much strategically. The reasoning given ('pass to my main phase to play more efficiently') is reasonable since there's no meaningful difference in timing here for Fact or Fiction - they can cast it at end of an opponent's turn later for more information. But casting it now during the draw step before making decisions could help inform the main phase plays.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Fact or Fiction now to see 5 more cards before making main phase decisions, since it's an instant and the mana would be available either way

However, discarding Zetalpa over cards like Swiftwater Cliffs (a tapland when they already have 8 lands) or Devil's Play (which requires a lot of mana to be impactful) could be questioned. That said, at 8 lands with no ramp, Zetalpa is very far from castable and the other cards have more immediate utility.

annotations.description: Casting Grave Pact with zero creatures on the battlefield means it does nothing immediately. Meanwhile, Gem25F ESPN has two Deep-Sea Krakens threatening lethal damage. With likely 10+ creature cards in all graveyards, Avatar of Woe could be cast for just BB, providing a 6/5 fear creature with tap-to-destroy ability, which directly addresses the Kraken threat. annotations.description: When splitting Fact or Fiction piles for Sonnet Gramps, putting zero cards in pile 1 means all 5 cards go in pile 2. The opponent simply chooses the pile with all 5 cards (Vorosh the Hunter, Skullbriar, Svogthos the Restless Tomb, and two Swamps), getting maximum value. This is the worst possible split.

Given Sonnet Gramps has Mimeoplasm as commander and many creatures in graveyard, keeping Vorosh (a strong copy target and 6/6 flyer) separated from the lands would force a real decision.

annotations.description: Grok4F Analyst has Swiftwater Cliffs on the stack (entering tapped), and chose to cast Fact or Fiction with their remaining mana. They have 8 lands but Dockside Extortionist is tapped, so available mana is likely 7 (Island, Plains, Myriad Landscape, Island, Plains, Plains, Mountain). Fact or Fiction costs 3U, leaving 3 mana. However, Jace's Sanctum costs 3U and would reduce future instant/sorcery costs by 1 and give scry triggers - casting it first would have made Fact or Fiction cost 3 instead of 4 on a future turn. But they can't cast both this turn (both cost 4). The real question is whether Fact or Fiction is better than Jace's Sanctum here. Fact or Fiction is reasonable as an end-of-turn-style play to dig for answers, but Jace's Sanctum would provide ongoing value with 8 instant/sorcery spells in hand. With Swiftwater Cliffs entering tapped, they'll have 8 mana sources next turn. Casting Jace's Sanctum now would let them cast discounted spells next turn. This is debatable - Fact or Fiction finds immediate answers and is an instant, so casting it during the main phase when they could wait until an opponent's end step is slightly suboptimal sequencing, though with Swiftwater Cliffs on the stack they may be responding during resolution. Actually, the choice is between Fact or Fiction and activating Myriad Landscape. Using Myriad Landscape to ramp would sacrifice it but get two basics, increasing future mana. Given they have expensive spells and need mana, this could be better long-term, but Fact or Fiction finding cards is also strong. This is close enough to be debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Fact or Fiction during postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Consider casting Jace's Sanctum instead to get cost reduction on the 7+ instants/sorceries in hand, or activate Myriad Landscape to ramp for future turns. Alternatively, if casting Fact or Fiction, wait until an opponent's end step for better information.

annotations.description: Storm Herd at 39 life is a potential game-winning card that creates 39 flying tokens. Meanwhile, the hand contains multiple flashback cards (Deep Analysis, Think Twice, Rolling Temblor, Devil's Play, Mass Diminish, Ray of Distortion) that retain most or all of their value when discarded to the graveyard. Discarding the win condition instead of flashback cards is a significant strategic error.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Storm Herd, a 39-token game-winning spell with no graveyard utility.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Storm Herd as a win condition and discard flashback cards like Deep Analysis, Think Twice, Rolling Temblor, Devil's Play, and Mass Diminish, which can all still be cast from the graveyard.

annotations.description: Gem25F ESPN has 8 mana available (4 Islands + Ur-Golem's Eye + Myriad Landscape) and two Deep-Sea Krakens already on board. Casting Mind Stone for 2 mana when already at 8+ mana is low-impact ramp that doesn't meaningfully advance the board state. Stormsurge Kraken (5 mana) would add a 5/5 hexproof threat alongside the two unblockable 6/6 Krakens, creating massive pressure. Alternatively, Shaper Parasite as a morph (3 mana) plus Mind Stone (2 mana) could be played together, but Stormsurge Kraken is the stronger play as it applies real pressure while opponents are weakened (GPT5m Timmy is dead, Grok4F at 39, Sonnet at 36). The Mind Stone is unnecessary ramp at this stage of the game when deploying threats would be more impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mind Stone (2 mana artifact for ramp/card draw later)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Stormsurge Kraken for 5 mana to add a powerful hexproof creature to the board alongside two unblockable Deep-Sea Krakens, then still have mana open for Pongify or Exclude as protection

annotations.description: Sonnet Gramps is at 36 life facing 36+ damage and chose not to block with any available creatures. If the attackers deal 36 damage and they have creatures that could block (Yavimaya Elder, Yavimaya Elder, Scythe Specter were listed as choices), not blocking means taking lethal damage. Even blocking two 6/6 Krakens would reduce incoming damage by 12, keeping them alive at 12 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to assign any blockers despite facing lethal damage
annotations.betterLine: Block two Deep-Sea Krakens with available creatures (Yavimaya Elders and/or Scythe Specter) to survive at 12 life, which also triggers Yavimaya Elder death triggers for card advantage and land searching

The extra Plains provides marginal ramp, but the card selection from Looting helps find the right cards from an already overflowing hand.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Faithless Looting from graveyard via flashback ({2}{R}) to draw 2 and discard 2, getting better card selection with 10 cards in hand while facing lethal unblockable threats.
